Rashi on Chullin 51b:10:1.hebrew: היכא דנפלה מן הגג - בלא ידעה, דאי ידעה — הא אמרינן דאמדה נפשה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:10:1.english: Where it fell from the roof - [This applies only] when it was unaware; for if it was aware, behold, we said that it braces itself.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:11:1.hebrew: כנגד בני מעיין - שמא נקרע רוב החיצונה, או ניקבו הדקין:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:11:1.english: Around the intestines - Lest the greater part of the outer [stomach wall] was torn, or the small intestines were perforated.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:11:2.english: Around the entire cavity - Due to [the concern of] the breaking of a majority of the ribs or the dislocation of vertebrae.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:12:1.hebrew: סימנין מאי - מי בעי בדיקה, שמא נעקרו:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:12:1.english: What about the simanim - Do they require inspection, lest they were torn loose?

Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:1.hebrew: עוף שנחבט - ונפל על כרחו על פני הנהר, ואיכא למיחש לריסוק:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:1.english: A bird that hit [the water] - And fell involuntarily upon the surface of the river, and there is concern for shattered limbs:

Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:2.english: Once it swims the full length of its [body] - It is [considered] like walking, which does not require inspection.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:3.english: And if [it is] standing water - Such as ponds.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:4.hebrew: לית לן בה - דאפילו מלמעלה למטה, שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:4.english: We have no [problem] with it - For even [if it swam] from above to below, it is acceptable.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:5.english: And if [one] cast chips of wood - And if there were chips of wood cast into the river:

Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:6.hebrew: וקדמיה - איהו לציבי מלמעלה למטה — אפילו במיא דלא קיימי, שרי; דכיון דקדמיה איהו לציבי, איהו דקא שט:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:13:6.english: And it overtook it - [If] it [overtook] the chips of wood [while moving] from above to below, even in water that is not standing, it is permitted; for since it overtook the chips of wood, it is [the bird itself] that is swimming.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:1.english: A garment - Spread over stakes in the air.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:2.english: And taut - Well [stretched], and a bird fell upon it:

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:3.hebrew: חיישינן - לריסוק, ובעי שהייה, דכיון דמתיח שפיר — קשה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:3.english: We must be concerned - For shattering [of the limbs], and it requires a waiting period; for since it is well taut, it is hard.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:4.hebrew: עוף ומעופף - ואם כפולה הטלית, ואפילו מתוחה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:4.english: Folded and doubled - And if the garment is folded, even if [it is] taut.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:5.english: We need not be concerned - For it does not stretch well.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:6.english: A net - A bird that fell into a net spread out in the air.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:7.english: If the knots are close together - The knots of the threads in it are consistently close to one another.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:14:8.english: We are concerned - Lest the knots crushed it.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:1.english: Flax arranged into bundles - Flax that is made into bundles.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:10.hebrew: דעביד ביזרי - פופיד"ש. אפילו דייק ונפיץ חיישינן, משום קטרי דאית ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:10.english: That was made into bundles - Poupées [bundles of flax]. Even [if] it was beaten and combed, we are concerned, because of the knots that are in it.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:11.hebrew: דקתא - נעורת, שברי גבעולין הננערין מן הפשתים כשמנפצין אותו:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:11.english: Tow - Tow, [namely,] fragments of stalks that are shaken out from the flax when one combs it.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:12.english: We must be concerned - If a bird fell upon them:

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:13.hebrew: דקדקתא - דקה מן הדקה, וגם היא נעורת:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:13.english: Fine tow - Finer than the fine [tow], and it too is tow.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:14.hebrew: לא חיישינן - אם יש ממנה כרי על גבי קרקע, ונופל עוף עליהן — לא חיישינן, לפי שהיא רכה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:14.english: We need not be concerned - If there is a pile of it on the ground and a bird falls upon them, we need not be concerned, because it is soft.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:2.english: We are concerned - For it is hard.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:3.hebrew: דהאי גיסא ודהאי גיסא - אם נפל על צדי החבילה מכאן ומכאן, בהשמטה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:3.english: [On] this side and [on] that side - If it fell on the sides of the bundle, on this side or that side, slipping off.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:4.hebrew: לא חיישינן - דכי מטי עלייהו, משתריק ומשתמיט, ולא מלקי ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:4.english: We need not be concerned - For when [the bird] reaches them, it slides and slips off, and [the impact] does not strike it.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:6.hebrew: כיתנא דדייק (ונפיץ) - חבוט, בטוד"ה בלע"ז:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:6.english: Flax that was beaten (and combed) - Beaten — batude in Old French.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:7.english: And shook itself - Escousse in Old French [shaking].

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:8.english: We are not concerned - If [it] is spread out on the ground and a bird falls upon it.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:15:9.english: [Flax that was] beaten but not combed - The fragments of the stalks injure the bird.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:1.hebrew: נברא - סיב הגדל סביב הדקלים, ומייבשין אותו, ונחלק לרצועות, ומפשילין ממנו חבלים. וכל זמן שלא נעשה רצועות, הוא קשה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:1.english: Nevara - The fiber that grows around palm trees; they dry it, and it splits into strips, and they twist ropes from it. And as long as it has not been made into strips, it is hard.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:2.hebrew: תימחתא - לאחר שחלקוהו לרצועות להאי נברא, כמו שעושין לקליפת עץ הקרוי טי"ל:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:2.english: Timchata - After one has split this *nivra* into strips, as is done with the bark of a tree called *til* [French *tille*, linden bast].

Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:3.hebrew: קיטמא נהילא - מרוקד בנפה, נכבש ונעשה קשה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:3.english: Sifted ashes - Sifted through a sieve; it becomes compacted and turns hard.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:4.hebrew: לא נהילא - אינו נכבש, וכל שעה הוא טפוף ואינו קשה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:16:4.english: Not sifted - It does not become compacted, and it is at all times loose and not hard.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:1:1.english: Becomes impure through ziva - If a discharge issues from him.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:1:2.hebrew: ואי ס"ד יש בו משום ריסוקי אברים - הרי חולה הוא, וזו אחד משבעה דרכים שהזב נבדק בהן, דזב אינו מטמא באונס; דכתיב (ויקרא טו) "זב מבשרו" — שיהא בשרו כמות שהוא שלם, ולא באונס:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:1:2.english: And if it should enter your mind that [a newborn] is subject to [the concern of] shattered limbs - Behold, he is ill, and this is one of seven ways in which a zav is examined, for a zav does not become impure through circumstances beyond his control; as it is written: “A discharge out of his flesh” (Leviticus 15:2) — that his flesh must be as it is, intact, and not [issuing discharge] due to circumstances beyond his control.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:2:1.hebrew: דרך דופן - ע"י סם, ובין הוא ובין אמו חיין. ואין לומר שלאחר שמתה אמו הוציאוהו, דקיי"ל במסכת נדה (דף מד.) — הוא מיית ברישא:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:2:1.english: By caesarean section - [This was done] by means of a drug, and both he and his mother are alive. And one cannot say that they extracted him after his mother died, for we maintain in tractate Niddah (44a) that [the fetus] dies first.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:3:1.hebrew: עגל שנולד בי"ט - אין כאן משום מוקצה, שהרי מוכן היה אגב אמו, ושוחטין אותו בו ביום. אלמא, משום ריסוקי אברים נמי לית ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:3:1.english: A calf that was born on a Festival - There is no [prohibition] here on account of muktzeh, for it was prepared along with its mother, and one may slaughter it on that very day. Evidently, there is no [concern] of shattered limbs in its case either.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:4:1.hebrew: ושוין - תנאי דפליגי במסכת ביצה (דף כו:) גבי בכור שנולד בו מום בי"ט. ושוין — דאפילו האוסר בנולד בו ביום מום, משום דמוקצה היה בין השמשות מחמת איסור קדשים בחוץ, אבל אם נולד היום ומומו עמו, מוכן הוא, שלא נאסר מעולם; דהא במעי אמו היה מוכן אגב אמו, ומותר — דבכור אינו קדוש עד שיולד, וכשנולד הרי מומו עמו, וראוי לישחט בחוץ:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:4:1.english: And they agree - [These are] the Tannaim who dispute in tractate Beitzah (26b) regarding a firstborn in which a blemish arose on a Festival. And they agree — that even the one who prohibits [in a case where] a blemish arose in it on that day, because it was muktzeh at twilight due to the prohibition of [slaughtering] consecrated animals outside [the Temple], yet if it was born today and its blemish [was born] with it, it is prepared, for it was never forbidden; for in its mother's womb it was prepared by virtue of its mother and permitted, since a firstborn is not sanctified until it is born, and when it was born, behold, its blemish was with it, and it is fit to be slaughtered outside [the Temple].

Rashi on Chullin 51b:4:2.hebrew: דרך דופן מי קדיש - בבכורה, דבעינן מום לישחט במדינה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:4:2.english: Is [an animal born by] caesarean section sanctified - [With the sanctity of] a firstborn, such that we would require a blemish [for it] to be slaughtered in the provinces?

Rashi on Chullin 51b:4:3.hebrew: מודה ר"ש - אע"ג דפליג במסכת נדה (דף מ.) גבי יוצא דופן, ואמר: הרי הוא כילוד ויושבת עליו ימי טומאה וטהרה — התם הוא דאיתרבאי מ"ואם נקבה תלד" לרבות יוצא דופן; אבל לענין קדשים מודה שאינו קדוש, דכתיב: "כי יולד" — פרט ליוצא דופן (לעיל חולין דף לח:):
Rashi on Chullin 51b:4:3.english: Rabbi Shimon concedes - Even though he disagrees in tractate Niddah (40a) regarding [an infant delivered via] caesarean section, and said, "It is considered born, and she observes the days of impurity and purity for it" — it is [only] there that it was included from [the verse], "And if she bears a female" (Leviticus 12:5), to include [an infant delivered via] caesarean section; but with regard to consecrated animals, he concedes that it is not sanctified, for it is written, "When it is born" (Leviticus 22:27) — excluding [an animal delivered via] caesarean section (above, Chullin 38b).

Rashi on Chullin 51b:5:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן - הא דקתני מותר בו ביום, ולא חייש לריסוק אברים:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:5:1.english: Here we are dealing with - [As for] that which is taught, [that it is] permitted on that [same] day, and [the Tanna] is not concerned about shattered limbs:

Rashi on Chullin 51b:5:2.hebrew: כגון שהפריס ע"ג קרקע - ננער לעמוד ותחב פרסותיו לעמוד, דאמרינן לקמן גבי נפולה: עמדה מנפילתה — אינה צריכה מעת לעת:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:5:2.english: For example, where it spread [its hooves] on the ground - It roused itself to stand and thrust its hooves [into the ground] to stand, as we say later regarding a fallen [animal]: [If] it stood up from its fall, it does not require twenty-four hours [of waiting].

Rashi on Chullin 51b:6:1.hebrew: בית המטבחים - כשמפילין אותו לארץ לשוחטו, אפילו ממקום גבוה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:6:1.english: The slaughterhouse - When they throw it to the ground to slaughter it, even from a high place.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:7:2.hebrew: קל גניחותיה - כמו (ב"ק דף פ.) גונח מלבו, פלינדרי"ש בלע"ז — שנשמע קול יללתו כשנפל:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:7:2.english: The sound of its groaning - As in (Bava Kamma 80a), "groaning from his heart," plaindres in Old French — that the sound of its wailing was heard when it fell.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:7:3.english: From where [did you learn] this? - That you are not concerned about [internal] crushing:

Rashi on Chullin 51b:7:4.hebrew: צפרניו נועץ - כשהוא שוהה ליפול, כל שעה הוא מתחזק בצפורניו, עד שאינו נופל מגובה:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:7:4.english: [The bull] digs in its claws - As it takes time to fall, all the while it braces itself with its claws, so that it does not fall from a height.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:8:1.hebrew: עמדה - אמתניתין קאי, שנפלה מן הגג: ועמדה ולא הלכה — אינה צריכה שהייה מעת לעת:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:8:1.english: Stood - It refers to the Mishnah, where [the animal] fell from the roof: and [if] it stood up but did not walk — it does not require waiting for a twenty-four-hour period.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:8:2.hebrew: אבל בדיקה בעיא - בחוט השדרה, ובשבירת רוב צלעות, ובעקירת חוליא. והיכא דלא עמדה, אפילו בדקנוה ונמצאת שלמה — טרפה, משום החבט שנתפרקו פרקיה וחוליותיה. ואם הלכה — אפילו בדיקה לא בעיא:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:8:2.english: But it requires inspection - In the spinal cord, and for a fracture of most of the ribs, and for the dislocation of a vertebra. And where it did not stand up, even if we inspected it and it was found intact, it is a tereifa because of the impact, as its joints and its vertebrae were dislocated. And if it walked, it does not even require inspection.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:9:1.hebrew: אע"ג דלא עמדה - ואינה צריכה שהייה מעת לעת:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:9:1.english: Even though it did not stand - And it does not require a twenty-four-hour waiting period.

Rashi on Chullin 51b:9:2.hebrew: ננערה לעמוד אע"פ - שלא פשטה ידה, אלא נתחזקה ורצתה לעמוד:
Rashi on Chullin 51b:9:2.english: It struggled to stand, even though - That it did not stretch out its foreleg, but rather braced itself and wanted to stand.

Tosafot on Chullin 51b:10:1.hebrew: והלכתא היכא דנפלה מן הגג כו' - הא דלא קאמר "הלכה כרב יהודה בריסוק אברים", משום דבעי לאשמועינן: דוקא עמדה — למעוטי פשטה ידה לעמוד וננערה לעמוד:
Tosafot on Chullin 51b:10:1.english: "And the halakha is: In any case where [an animal] fell from the roof, etc." - The reason that [the Gemara] did not say: "The halakha is in accordance with Rav Yehuda regarding crushed limbs," is because it wanted to teach us [that it is] specifically [if] it stood, to exclude [the cases where] it stretched out its foreleg to stand and [where] it shook itself to stand.

Tosafot on Chullin 51b:4:1.hebrew: מודה רבי שמעון לענין קדשים - לא הוה צריך כאן לדברי רבי יוחנן, דבבכור עסקינן — דתלי רחמנא בפטר רחם. וקדשים גופייהו לא יליף ר"ש אלא מבכור, "לידה" "לידה", כדאמר בריש יוצא דופן (נדה דף מ.). ולרבותא נקט הכא כל קדשים:
Tosafot on Chullin 51b:4:1.english: Rabbi Shimon concedes with regard to consecrated animals - [The Gemara] did not need Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement here, as we are dealing with a firstborn, which the Merciful One conditioned upon the opening of the womb; and consecrated animals themselves Rabbi Shimon derived only from a firstborn [via the verbal analogy of] "birth" [and] "birth," as it says at the beginning of Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 40a). And it mentioned all consecrated animals here for the sake of the greater novelty.

Tosafot on Chullin 51b:8:1.hebrew: עמדה אינה צריכה מעת לעת אבל בדיקה ודאי בעיא - אבל לא עמדה, בעיא ודאי מעת לעת, ובעיא נמי בדיקה, כדתנן לקמן (חולין דף נו.): "דרסה וטרפה בכותל או שריצצתה בהמה — צריך מעת לעת"; ואמר בגמרא משום ר"א בר' ינאי: "אחת זו ואחת זו צריכה בדיקה". וא"ת: והא תניא בפ' התערובת (בזבחים דף ע:): "נתערבה בשור שנעבדה בו עבירה, בכלאים, ובטרפה..."; ובגמרא (דף עד:) פריך: "האי טרפה היכי דמי? אי דידע ליה — לשקלה, אי דלא ידע ליה — מנא ידע?", ומשני ר"ל: "דאיערב בנפולה"; ופריך: "בנפולה — לבדקיה!", ומשני: "קסבר: עמדה — צריכה מעת לעת, הלכה — צריכה בדיקה". והשתא, על כרחך עיקר שינויא לא הוי מ"עמדה צריכה מעת לעת", דאכתי ליבדקיה בהילוך! ועוד, דכיון דמעת לעת סגי, אמאי קתני: "ירעו עד שיסתאבו"? אלא עיקר שינויא — מ"הלכה צריכה בדיקה". וכיון דאין מרויח שום דבר במה שאומר "עמדה צריכה מעת לעת", ל"ל למימר הכי? הא כ"ע מודו הכא דעמדה אינה צריכה מעת לעת! ונראה דגרסי' התם: "עמדה אינה צריכה מעת לעת"; אע"ג דלא צריך ליה התם, נקטיה אגב "הלכה בעיא בדיקה":
Tosafot on Chullin 51b:8:1.english: "If it stood, it does not require a twenty-four-hour period, but it certainly requires inspection" - However, if it did not stand up, it certainly requires a twenty-four-hour period, and it also requires inspection, as we learned in a mishna later (Chullin 56a): "[If a person] trampled it or slammed it against a wall, or an animal crushed it... it requires a twenty-four-hour period"; and [the Gemara on 56b] says in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai: "Both this and that require inspection." And if you will say: But isn't it taught [in a baraita] in the chapter [entitled] HaTa'arovot (Zevachim 70b): "If [a consecrated animal] became mixed with an ox with which a transgression was committed, or with [an animal of] kilayim, or with a tereifa..." [they must graze until they become blemished]? And in the Gemara (74b) it asks: "What are the circumstances of this tereifa? If he knows [which one] it is, let him take it out; if he does not know [which one] it is, from where does he know [that a tereifa is mixed in]?" And Reish Lakish answers: "Where it became mixed with a fallen animal." And it asks: "With regard to a fallen animal, let him inspect it [by seeing if it can stand and walk]!" And it answers: "He holds: [If] it stood, it requires a twenty-four-hour period; [if] it walked, it requires inspection." And now, perforce the primary resolution is not based on "[if] it stood, it requires a twenty-four-hour period," for he could still inspect it by [seeing if it] walks! And furthermore, since a twenty-four-hour period would be sufficient, why does [the baraita] teach: "They shall graze until they become blemished"? Rather, the primary resolution is from "[even if] it walked, it requires inspection." And since he gains nothing at all by saying "[if] it stood, it requires a twenty-four-hour period," why did he need to say this? For everyone here [in Chullin] agrees that [if] it stood, it does not require a twenty-four-hour period! And it appears that we should read there [in Zevachim]: "[If] it stood, it does not require a twenty-four-hour period"; [and] even though it was not needed there, [the Gemara] formulated it along with "[even if] it walked, it requires inspection."
